fields.Intro Paragraph 1: What if everyone knew that religion was never about real people, but symbolized natural forces? The geopolitical ramifications of scriptural literalism have never been more evident, as our analysis of Aaron Exodus, and the Golden Calf demonstrates.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In this episode of Inner Whirled, we take another swing at exposing the symbolic framework behind mythology that masquerades as history. Drawing on the work of Rev. Robert Taylor and our own research, we demonstrate how figures like Moses and Jesus represent natural, celestial, and hydrological forces, especially the relationship between the sun and water. From the "blood of the river" to modern baptism, we show how greased up priests and their anointing oils have misconstrued metaphors for millennia, turning real world wisdom into superstitious belief systems. In Part 2 we enter the rarely explored territory of the uncomfortable connection between the golden calf, money, kingship, and a system of symbols that still plasters power structures today. Is Moses linguistically connected to the calf? Where does Taurus show up in coinage, cathedrals, and scripture? And the biggest question: was history itself constructed from this same symbolic system in the relatively recent past?

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Money as the Universal God", "body": "Taylor's argument is that calf worship never ended, it only changed address, and the exclusive hour opens with him pointing at a country where the golden calf still sits in gold beneath the inscription Deo gratia rex, where rex and basileus are both old titles of the sun and the sun never dies. The ancient coins of Crete and Athens carried a calf or bull's head as the object of idolatry, and from the general word for cattle we get pecuniary, so religious matters and pecuniary matters turn out to be two names for one thing."}, {"title": "A Nation Missing From the Record", "body": "Before Taylor is allowed to argue about Israel's kings, the hosts stop to say that no metals, royalty or theocracy referring to Israel have ever been brought out of the ancient world, and the caduceus and bull symbolism dated between 133 and 103 BC is credited to a nation that leaves no archaeological trace. The method on display is debunking the presumption rather than arguing inside the story, and the same move recurs all hour, from the basilisk being nothing but a little king to Mitzrayim being quietly translated as Egypt when the letters say something else."}, {"title": "The Calf Was Always Taurus", "body": "Aaron sets his calf in Horeb, Jeroboam sets two in Bethel and Dan, and Taylor argues these are not separate places but names for the same mansion of the sun, the constellation we call Taurus, identified by the Pleiades in its forehead and by the red star Aldebaran. Horeb is unpacked as light plus the green shoots of spring, the season for sowing. The chain closes at St Paul's Cathedral, where the calf couchant at the foot of St Luke shows only head, shoulders and forelegs, exactly as the zodiacal bull is drawn."}, {"title": "A Sky Map Younger Than It Looks", "body": "The most destructive claim in the second hour is that Ptolemy's Almagest, the oldest text describing the modern eighty eight constellations, contains positions that can only correspond to Renaissance dates, which anyone can check in Stellarium. Put that beside the Decree of Canopus, dated to 238 BC but thoroughly Alexandrian, beside a Coptic alphabet that is simply rearranged Greek, and beside the centuries when these cathedrals and their evangelist carvings were being built, and the antiquity everyone rests on starts to look like something assembled all at once."}, {"title": "Cipher Alphabets and an Italian Origin", "body": "Hebrew is described as an alphabet with no utility, hard to track letter by letter, built as a code for initiates rather than a common language, and hieroglyphs are read the same way, which is why they can only be translated through a fairly recent Coptic. Against that, the alphabets that do look old lead back to Italy, to the Abecedaria found there that turned out to be Etruscan, to the runes traced out of Clusium, to Pelasgian polygonal masonry and a porphyry coffer, and to the suggestion that the Great Pyramid was an Italian industry, a temple of Janus."}]
